comparison: Both agree on the temporal correlation between reproduction and exopher production (C2, C3, C32). OpenEval also evaluates FUdR suppression effects (C35-C36) which peer reviewers accept as part of the broader genetic evidence but don't separately discuss.

Both support the genetic dissection findings. OpenEval specifically evaluates glp-4(ts) system (C4, C40-C41), while peer reviewers group this with broader genetic evidence (C4-C7, C41, C44-C51) praising the systematic approach as 'thorough and solid.'

Both support genetic evidence that sperm alone are insufficient (C6, C43-C46). OpenEval evaluates this as a separate finding, while peer reviewers treat it as part of the comprehensive genetic battery distinguishing direct from indirect effects.

Both support the dual requirement for sperm and oocytes (C5, C48-C51). OpenEval treats this as distinct evidence, while peer reviewers incorporate it into their overall assessment of the genetic dissection as 'very convincing.'

Both evaluate eggshell component RNAi experiments (C57-C62). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to confounding of eggshell integrity with early embryonic events (C61), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting it as part of the systematic genetic approach without raising the confounding concern.

Both support the mating rescue experiment (C8, C64-C68). OpenEval emphasizes the experimental design distinguishing egg presence from chronological age, while peer reviewers note this as part of evidence that 'shifting the timing of egg production and egg laying alters the onset of observed exophers.'

Both strongly support single-copy transgene validation (C9, C69-C74). OpenEval notes consistency across approaches strengthens conclusions, while peer reviewers explicitly state this 'addressed the main weakness' by showing exophers are not artifacts of mCherry overexpression.

Both support pharmacological manipulation experiments (C78-C79, C81-C82). OpenEval notes the 5-HT experiment uses fasting conditions adding complexity, while peer reviewers emphasize 'pharmacological manipulation of egg laying has the predicted effects' as part of complementary approaches.

Both support spatial correlation between neuron position and exopher production (C83-C88). OpenEval notes 70% baseline positioning suggests additional factors, while peer reviewers emphasize 'clear bias toward neurons whose cell bodies are adjacent to the filled uterus' as key evidence for mechanical force.

Both evaluate rol-6 positioning experiments (C89-C91, C93-C94). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to unexplained high baseline (~40%) in rol-6 animals as confounding factor, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, focusing on dramatic positional effects without addressing the baseline concern.

Both support differential effects on touch neurons based on proximity (C92). OpenEval notes this provides strong correlative evidence, while peer reviewers incorporate this into their assessment that spatial relationship is 'key evidence for mechanical force.'

Both support correlation between uterine length and exopher production (C10-C11, C97-C100, C119). OpenEval notes measurements are absolute rather than normalized to body length, while peer reviewers accept this as 'supporting evidence for the mechanical model' without raising normalization concerns.

Both strongly support dead embryo experiments (C12-C13, C103-C107). OpenEval calls this 'critical experiment' distinguishing chemical signals from physical distention, while peer reviewers state experiments provide 'convincing evidence that exopher production is driven by stretch-dependent feedback.'

Both strongly support oocyte retention experiments (C12, C112-C115). OpenEval emphasizes this supports mechanical distention over chemical signaling from embryos, while peer reviewers note 'ability of various uterine contents to induce exophers is viewed as key evidence.'

Both support experiments removing uterine contents (C116-C118). OpenEval calls this 'critical control experiment' strengthening uterine filling hypothesis, while peer reviewers incorporate it into evidence that 'embryos lacking an intact eggshell with reduced rigidity have impaired exopher production.'

Both support correlation analysis (C119). OpenEval notes strong correlation (r=0.8839) but emphasizes correlation doesn't establish causation and would benefit from body length normalization, while peer reviewers accept this as part of supporting evidence without methodological concerns.

Both support microinjection experiments (C14, C120-C123). OpenEval notes modest ~20% induction rate and potential chemical effects of dye as limitations, while peer reviewers view this as 'very interesting' and 'strong direct evidence for mechanical force' with vulva control supporting mechanical interpretation.

Both evaluate the central conclusion about mechanical force (C15-C16, C124-C127). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting evidence supports role but doesn't definitively exclude chemical signaling or prove necessity, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED with 'compelling evidence' that uterine distension induces vesicular extrusion.

Both accept background claims about exophers and prior work (C1, C17-C30). OpenEval notes these are supported by citations establishing biological context, while peer reviewers accept without question as they are based on published work and not the focus of evaluation.

OpenEval supports background claims (C1, C30) as establishing context, while peer reviewer R16 raises UNCERTAINTY specifically about biological significance and connection to pathology, stating 'Whether this process is related to the extrusion of cellular damage...should be addressed in future studies.'

Both accept contextual claims about reproduction and FUdR (C31-C34, C37-C39). OpenEval notes these are supported by citations and established knowledge, while peer reviewers accept as established facts from prior literature providing necessary biological context.

Both accept established C. elegans reproductive biology facts (C42, C47, C52-C56, C63). OpenEval notes these are well-established from literature providing essential context, while peer reviewers accept without question as established facts not requiring evaluation.

Both accept contextual claims about serotonin and genetics (C75-C77, C80). OpenEval notes these provide context for pharmacological experiments, while peer reviewers accept as established facts from prior literature.

Both support observational claims about tissue distortion (C95-C96). OpenEval notes this provides visual evidence for mechanical hypothesis, while peer reviewers accept as straightforward documentation that 'egg production and accumulation have dramatic consequences to the viscera.'

Both accept contextual claims about dead eggs and oocyte biology (C101, C108-C111). OpenEval notes these provide context for interpreting experiments, while peer reviewers accept as established facts from prior literature.

Both accept claims about C. elegans reproductive biology and mechanotransduction context (C128-C131). OpenEval notes these provide context for discussing potential mechanisms, while peer reviewers accept as established facts.

Both support inferences ruling out alternative mechanical force sources (C132-C137). OpenEval notes logic is sound though alternatives not exhaustively tested, while peer reviewers accept as reasonable interpretations with sound logic, noting molecular mechanism remains unknown.

Both support mechanotransduction speculation (C138-C142). OpenEval notes these are appropriately presented as hypotheses for future work, while peer reviewers accept as reasonable discussion points, explicitly noting 'main weakness is that it does not explore the molecular mechanism.'

Both support rapid response observation (C143-C144). OpenEval notes implications for understanding mechanotransduction mechanism, while peer reviewers note 'acute injection...causes a similar induction of exopher release' as part of direct evidence.

Both support comparative context about mechanosensing in reproduction (C145-C147). OpenEval notes this suggests broad conservation, while peer reviewers accept as reasonable discussion providing comparative context.

Both evaluate speculation about muscle exophers and tissue-wide licensing (C148-C152). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation goes beyond data and requires experimental support, while peer reviewers accept as appropriate speculation recognizing it as future work.

Both evaluate speculation about HSF-1 regulation (C153-C159). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting connection between HSF-1 and exopher production not directly tested, while peer reviewers accept as reasonable discussion points appropriate for speculation about future work.

Both support speculation about temporal patterns and reproductive decline (C160-C165). OpenEval notes speculation is appropriately qualified, while peer reviewers accept as reasonable hypotheses based on temporal patterns observed.

Both support broader mechanobiology context (C166-C169). OpenEval notes these provide broader context for mechanobiology findings, while peer reviewers accept as reasonable discussion providing field context.

Both support discussion of implications for neurodegenerative disease (C170-C174). OpenEval notes connection is appropriately qualified as inviting further consideration, while peer reviewers accept as reasonable discussion points with appropriate qualification.
